The APK has 985 file entries, no explicit directory entries, 41,007,977 uncompressed member bytes, and passes ZIP integrity checks.

The manifest declares INTERNET and ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE, launcher activity uit.dev.pencilblade.PencilBlade, and Google Ads AdActivity, with no service, receiver, or provider.

claim: The APK contains only lib/armeabi/libgame.so; it is a stripped ELF32 little-endian ARM EABI5 shared object with CPU architecture v5TE.
Embedded native strings identify Cocos2d-x 2.1.4 and the PencilBlade project path.
The APK has 784 PNG under assets, 107 PNG under res, 59 WAV, 3 MP3, 15 TTF, 1 OTF, and 392 files in each resolution tree.
No asset filename uses plist, JSON, XML, TMX, CCBI, Lua, JavaScript, or CSV extensions, so no external level or gameplay configuration is present in those formats.
Surviving native dynamic symbols expose six named modes plus gameplay, scoring, timing, objectives, settings, and persistence systems.
PhysicsLayer creates a Box2D world with gravity (0.0, -10.0) and enables sleeping.
notes: GNU ARM objdump and LLVM objdump in explicit Thumbv5TE mode agree on the instruction stream. The b2Vec2 literal is 0x00000000, 0xC1200000; SetAllowSleeping receives true.

claim: PhysicsLayer initializes velocity and position iterations to 10, initializes world-speed scale to 1.0, and calls b2World::Step(deltaTime * worldSpeed, velocityIterations, positionIterations) while the world is active.
notes: Both disassemblers agree. Constructor literal 0x41200000 is 10.0 for both iteration fields; 0x3F800000 is 1.0. update converts the iteration fields to integers before b2World::Step.

claim: PhysicsLayer::FreezeeWorld sets the world-speed multiplier to 0.5, UnFreezeeWorld restores 1.0, and SetWorldSpeed stores the supplied multiplier.
notes: The method name spelling is preserved from the native symbol. Constants are 0x3F000000 and 0x3F800000.

claim: The Android persistence path routes Cocos2d-x CCUserDefault typed operations through JNI to SharedPreferences named Cocos2dxPrefsFile; legacy UserDefault.xml is a separate read/migration path.
notes: Java setters commit synchronously. The double adapter stores a Java float; CCUserDefault::flush is a no-op on this path.

claim: Settings::SaveData writes 50 integer and four boolean preference keys; Settings::LoadData supplies recovered defaults for currency, selections, best scores, item prices, objective progress, audio/effect options, network sentinel, and rated state.
notes: The exact key/default table and indexed objectives_value_%d and mode_unlock_%d families are recorded in forensics/native/java-jni-boundary.md.

claim: The native gameplay physics paths use 32 legacy Cocos world units per Box2D metre, synchronize positions with metres multiplied by 32, and step gravity (0,-10) with 10 velocity and 10 position iterations.
notes: These paths call getWinSize rather than getWinSizeInPixels. Cocos Creator accepts world-unit inputs and applies its own PTM 32 conversion; the Creator gravity boundary is (0,-320) world units per second squared.

claim: Classic Fruit and Bomb factories create dynamic bodies with recovered shape formulas, density 1, friction 0.2, restitution 0, non-sensor fixtures, and bilateral category/mask filters that reject normal Fruit-Fruit, Bomb-Bomb, and Fruit-Bomb contacts.
notes: Fruit IDs 1 and 2 use box half-extents width/32 and height/32 metres; other valid Fruit IDs use circle radius (width+height)/128; Bomb radius is width/88.

claim: BombElectric assigns node tag 1437 and creates a disabled static body with a zero-height box fixture, category 0x0003 and mask 0x0002, then installs an electric contact listener.
notes: The native PreSolve path uses an incompatible object-layout access. Its runtime impact is unknown; the Creator rewrite must remain type-safe and treat behavior beyond the recovered fixture/filter facts as a reviewed compatibility decision.

claim: Toss randomness lazily seeds the process-global lrand48 stream from time(NULL); integer ranges are inclusive and nextFloat returns exactly one of the ten deciles 0.0 through 0.9.
notes: Exact native draw interleaving with Cocos/VFX lrand48 consumers remains unknown, so Creator tests use an injected scripted RNG without claiming original sequence parity.

claim: Classic constructs and concurrently runs a fixed graph of nine Free, Concurrent, and Wave toss controllers with recovered intervals, strict greater-than timer expiry, object types, directions, start/stop order, and spawn kinematic formulas.
notes: The exact table and RNG-consumption order are recorded in the toss contract. Concurrent intentionally samples through countMax+1 because it passes max+1 to an inclusive helper.

claim: Classic blade input owns four touch slots and, after the physics step, extends each active segment by trunc(viewportWidth/16), raycasts forward and reverse through all fixtures, applies the recovered tag/disabled/fruit filters, and performs no value-level fixture deduplication.
notes: The cut callback receives the original unextended segment. Creator ray endpoints stay in world units because Creator applies PTM conversion internally.

claim: Fruit scores 1 normally and 10 when critical; Classic fruit ID 13 starts BombElectric and submits 10, ID 14 starts the magnet presentation and submits 10, and other IDs submit the supplied Fruit score.
notes: The fruit-ID semantic comes from the complete Fruit::getID to notification to ClassicModeLayer::FruitCut caller chain.

claim: Classic combo scoring uses a rolling 0.25-second window; once the elapsed gap is greater than 0.25 seconds, clusters of at least three fruit cuts add a bonus equal to the cut count and smaller clusters add no combo bonus.
notes: Accepted order is objective event, combo-item creation, score, attach, conditional sound, reset. Effects enabled consumes one shared RandomHelper sound draw; disabled consumes none. Each fruit's own score is separate.

claim: Double score becomes active immediately, accumulates signed score in a pending bucket during a 1-second intro and 15-second delay, then clears the flag and flushes pending multiplied by two through normal AddScore.
notes: Early disable uses the same pending-times-two flush path.

claim: Classic queues one fail indicator callback per first-three missed fruits; every outstanding callback that completes while the count is exactly three invokes the registered game-over callback, while guarded Classic GameOver keeps the terminal transition idempotent. BombHit disables cuts, stops all nine toss controllers and BombElectric, stops physics, submits -10, and later calls guarded GameOver before resuming physics.
notes: FailCallback has no consumed guard, so callback invocation count depends on action completion order. The bomb Boolean virtual resolves to PhysicsLayer::StopPhysicsWorld(bool); a pending fail callback may arm GameOver during the bomb hold.

claim: Standard Classic reports mode 0, owns no TimeManager, leaves cut input enabled throughout the nominal 1.5-second Good/Luck intro, and starts its nine toss controllers only when the Luck sequence completes.
notes: StartGameCallback redundantly calls DisableCut(false) before consuming the initial toss-controller RNG draws; no countdown service belongs to standard Classic.

claim: Classic arms a 30-second world-speed action at scene entry; each callback adds float32 0.1 while the pre-add speed is below 2.0 and rearms after every addition. Pause takes effect after its 0.25-second entrance action, while resume restarts the director before its 0.25-second exit action.
notes: World speed scales only the Box2D step delta. Director pause suppresses scheduler and action progress without resetting controller, timer, explosion, or terminal state.

claim: A Classic bomb hit stops physics before applying -10; its explosion runs a 0.25-second delay, a 1.0-second full-rect white quad, and 1.25 seconds of white triangles, then calls guarded GameOver before resuming physics. Terminal guard, pending fail callbacks, and distinct same-query bomb explosions are independent.
notes: The physics-stop flag is last-writer, not reference-counted. Multiple distinct bombs admitted by one collected ray may overlap; duplicate reports for one bomb are blocked by its per-object guard.

claim: The shared TimeManager used by timed modes has independently recovered schedule, countdown, warning, expiry, callback, freeze, and thaw behavior; Start only schedules, Stop only unschedules, and Restart resets only remaining time and warning second.
notes: Standard Classic does not instantiate this service. Native callbacks are synchronous and mostly unguarded; any Creator hardening is an explicit compatibility decision.
